A 2.2 km bore. A 563 m elevation change. One of the longest HDDs the industry has ever attempted.
Michels Trenchless just finished a major piece of work at Snowy 2.0 in the Kosciuszko area of NSW. The Marica Road crossing came in at 2,248 metres with a 563 metre elevation drop. Most HDDs deal with around 50 metres of grade change. This one was more than ten times that.

They used two custom rigs, nearly 400 tonnes of push and pull each, and a pilot-hole intersect through hard rock.

Bores like that put the fluid program under real pressure. Long strings mean more rods in the hole. More rods mean more friction. Friction is what spikes your torque, slows your pull, and stresses the gear.

Across Australia and New Zealand the bores are getting longer. Infrastructure projects, deep geothermal, urban crossings. The ground is the same. The lengths are not.
Bores getting longer on your jobs too? What is changing in your fluid program to keep up?

Long bores do not get hard because the ground changes. They get hard because of friction.
Picture the string at 1,500 metres. Every joint of rod is dragging against the wall of the bore. Every metre adds load. The drive head feels it as torque. The puller feels it as pressure on the head.

That friction is what cooks rigs, slows progress, and gives crews stuck pipe nightmares.

The job of the fluid is not just to carry cuttings out. It is also to put a film between the rods and the ground so the string slides instead of grinds.

That is what a drill string lubricant does. It is added to the fluid program when you know the bore is going to be long, tight, or sticky. The mud still needs to do the carry and stability work. The lube takes the friction off the steel.

This Friday we will go deeper on Torque Down, our drill string lubricant. When to add it. When not to. What it pairs with.
What is your go-to when the torque starts climbing on a long pull? Add more fluid? Pump faster? Lube it up?

If your torque gauge is climbing on every long pullback, you are paying for it. In time, in rods, in wear.
Torque Down is the drill string lubricant in the Blick Fluids range. It rides along inside your fluid program and puts a slick film on the steel. Less drag on the rods. Less load on the drive. Less heat on the bearings.

Where it earns its keep:
• Long bores where the string is dragging through the whole hole
• Tight pullbacks where the product is fighting the wall the whole way
• Sticky or reactive ground that grips the rods
• Hard rock where the gear is already working hard

What it does not do: it does not replace your gel or your fluid loss product. The mud still has to carry, suspend, and seal. Torque Down sits on top of that program, not in place of it.

For dosage on your specific job, give one of our team a call. The right rate depends on the ground, the length, and what else is in your fluid. We will help you dial it in.

Less torque. Cleaner bores. Longer life on your gear.
Got a long pullback coming up? Call us before the rig leaves the yard. We will look at the program with you.
